newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mayors oppose moratorium on Internet taxation.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mayors oppose moratorium on Internet taxation.

text.p: U.S. mayors Tuesday opposed federal legislation that would prevent state and local governments from slapping new taxes on Internet transactions.
The U.S. Conference of Mayors, meeting in San Francisco, adopted the policy resolution by Chicago Mayor Richard Daley and Dallas Mayor Ronald Kirk with no debate.
The resolution opposes the establishment of an unlimited moratorium on state and local government taxation of electronic transactions.
It also urged the Clinton administration and Congress to delay taking action on the issue until "thorough and impartial" studies were completed.

Earlier this year, Representative Christopher Cox, R-Calif., and Sen. Ron Wyden, D-Ore., introduced identical bills that would impose an indefinite moratorium on state and local taxation of commerce over the Internet.
The legislation would not affect existing taxes on goods and services ordered through the Internet, as long as the taxes were the same as those on mail order goods.
At a congressional hearing last month, Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers said the administration strongly supports the "goals and underlying objectives" of the legislation.
U.S. mayors at the conference said the bill would intrude on their powers and create budget problems.
"The U.S. Conference of Mayors supports the growth of legitimate, wholesome commerce on the Internet," the resolution said.
But it added; "The proposed federal legislation would create a virtually unprecedented intrusion into inherently local affairs."
